title: Investigate GPU memory fragmentation and cudaMallocAsync pooling causing KV cache growth
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Symptom: Long-running inference processes with continuous batching and large KV caches slowly increase resident GPU memory over days, eventually hitting OOMs despite no obvious reference leaks in Python. Suspected cause: allocator behavior (cudaMallocAsync + pool) + fragmentation amplified by varying sequence-length workloads and frequent small allocations from KV cache growth and pooling heuristics. This ticket tracks root-cause investigation, reproducible test creation, instrumentation, and mitigation (pool tuning / periodic compact / allocation path changes).
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy dedicated-runtime image with continuous-batching enabled and default cudaMallocAsync pooling (pool limit: 20 GiB) in test cluster
Run synthetic workload: 100 concurrent streams, sequence-length distribution: 128 (40%), 384 (40%), 1024 (20%), 24h run
Enable KV cache warmup by sending repeated long-context conversations to create large KV entries
Monitor nvidia-smi, DCGM metrics, and process RSS for GPU, capturing snapshots every 30m
Observe steady increase in allocated GPU memory and fragmentation metrics in nvml samples, with occasional spikes on large-batch steps
investigation_notes: Initial profiling with nvprof and Nsight Systems shows many small allocations from runtime KV growth and internal CUDA kernels for attention caches
cudaMallocAsync pool shows many sub-allocations and scatter of free blocks; pool statistics via cuMemPoolGetAttribute indicate high fragmentation ratio on larger sequence steps
cuda-memcheck did not show leaks on the CUDA API layer, suggesting allocations are accounted but not reusable due to fragmentation / alignment constraints
Observed allocator behavior: when a requested size doesn't fit existing free blocks, cudaMallocAsync falls back to fresh device allocations instead of coalescing, increasing total resident memory
Reproducer added: stress_alloc.cu (micro-benchmark) that simulates KV cache allocate/free patterns and mirrors fragmentation seen in the runtime

Hypothesis: frequent variable-size allocations from KV growth + pooling bucketization cause leftover holes that cannot be reused due to differing alignment and size buckets. Continuous batching mixes different sequence lengths leading to churn.
Telemetry: added pool metrics emission (pool_total_bytes, pool_free_bytes, pool_fragmentation_pct) to the console traces; preliminary dashboard at /console/runtime/gpu-pools (internal link)
proposed_changes: Short-term mitigation: configure pool trimming interval to 5min and enable conservative pooling (larger bucket granularity) on dedicated nodes with mixed sequence workloads
Implement periodic compaction pass: attempt to coalesce freed pool segments and release back to OS/GPU when fragmentation exceeds threshold
Long-term: switch KV cache allocator to use slab allocator for fixed-size KV chunk objects to reduce variable-sized allocation churn
Add alignment-aware allocation: normalize KV allocations to common power-of-two sizes to improve reuse across sequence-length variants
Add synthetic e2e regression test in ci/perf that runs stress_alloc reproducer for 8h and fails on >5% bloat compared to baseline
Instrument runtime to emit allocation stack traces for large new device allocations to correlate with code paths (sampled, rate-limited)
Prototype fallback for when cudaMallocAsync returns a new device allocation: try to compact small free blocks first before allocating new memory
acceptance_criteria: Reproducer run (8h, mixed sequences) shows <2% growth in resident GPU memory compared to baseline after applying mitigations
No OOMs triggered in dedicated CI cluster for 72h under continuous-batching load after changes
Console dashboard shows pool_fragmentation_pct reduced by >50% under sample workload
Changes landed in runtime-2.4 and validated on a staging dedicated pool with canary rollout and rollback plan
Documentation updated: runtime/gpu-memory.md including guidance for pool tuning and KV cache sizing
qa_steps: Deploy patched runtime to staging dedicated pool with canary (10% nodes) and run synthetic workload for 48h
Verify telemetry: pool metrics, nvml snapshots, per-request latency and p95 does not regress >5%
Run e2e with variable sequence-length distribution and confirm KV cache eviction still functional and correctness maintained
Trigger simulated node reclamation and confirm compaction does not block inference threads longer than 200ms (sampled)
